content: Croflemer has the potential to inhibit the enzyme CYP3A4 at concentrations expected in the gastrointestinal tract. However, due to its minimal systemic absorption, it is unlikely to inhibit CYP3A4 systemically. This property necessitates caution and monitoring when co-administered with drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. Croflemer increases the levels of methylprednisolone by affecting its metabolism through hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzymes. This interaction requires careful monitoring to avoid potential adverse effects. Croflemer decreases the systemic absorption of intranasal metoclopramide when co-administered with drugs that impair gastrointestinal motility. This may reduce the therapeutic efficacy of metoclopramide, necessitating close monitoring. Croflemer increases the levels of midazolam by inhibiting its metabolism via CYP3A4. This interaction may lead to prolonged sedation, especially when co-administered with mild CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitoring is advised.
